answer:
Use LDA pseudopotentials from the PseudoDojo SRv0.4.1 standard set, specifically bi.upf, fe.upf, and o.upf from the PseudoDojo/SR_v0.4.1/LDA_standard directory.
Build the starting BiFeO3 structure in the R3c space group (hexagonal setting) with 10 atoms per primitive cell (two BiFeO3 formula units), placing Bi on Wyckoff 6a, Fe on Wyckoff 6a, and O on Wyckoff 18b, and using the canonical R3c literature lattice parameters a ≈ 5.58 Å and c ≈ 13.87 Å as the initial guess for the cell.
Run the calculation as spin-polarized with nspin = 2 and enforce G-type antiferromagnetic ordering on the Fe sublattice (Fe³⁺ high-spin d⁵), consistent with the known magnetic ground state of R3c BiFeO3.
Initialize the Fe magnetic moments to opposite signs using starting_magnetization(Fe) = +0.5 μB on one Fe atom in the primitive cell and starting_magnetization(Fe) = -0.5 μB on the other, and set starting_magnetization(Bi) = 0.0 and starting_magnetization(O) = 0.0.
Perform a variable-cell relaxation (vc-relax) with etot_conv_thr = 1.0e-8, forc_conv_thr = 1.0e-7, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8 for both the electronic and ionic steps, allowing the cell shape, cell volume, and atomic positions to relax.
Use a plane-wave kinetic energy cutoff ecutwfc = 60 Ry and a charge density cutoff ecutrho = 480 Ry (eight times ecutwfc) for both the relaxation and the subsequent SCF.
Sample the Brillouin zone with an automatic Monkhorst-Pack grid of 6 × 6 × 6 and a half-shift offset of (0.5, 0.5, 0.5), applied uniformly to the vc-relax and the SCF.
Use fixed occupations (occupations = "fixed") with no thermal smearing, since BiFeO3 is a large-gap insulator in LDA and no degauss value is required.
After the vc-relax converges, take the fully relaxed lattice vectors and atomic coordinates and run a final single-point self-consistent field calculation with the same pseudopotentials, cutoffs, k-points, spin/magnetic settings, and conv_thr = 1.0e-8 to produce the converged total energy.
Return the fully relaxed hexagonal R3c cell (lattice vectors a, b, c and the associated internal parameters of Bi, Fe, and O) together with the final total energy of the SCF run expressed in Rydbergs.
